deep.reconstruction:
The page holds five unrelated pieces of work.

(1) 'Verwandlung' (transformation) of a continued fraction.
Write K(α,β,γ;x) for the continued fraction on the left:
K = 1/(1 − k1 x/(1 − k2 x/(1 − k3 x/(1 − …)))), with
- k1 = αβ/(γ(γ+1)),
- k2 = (γ+1−α)(γ+1−β)/((γ+1)(γ+2)),
- k3 = (α+1)(β+1)/((γ+2)(γ+3)),
- and so on alternately.
This is Gauss's continued fraction for F(a,b+1;c+1;x)/F(a,b;c;x), with partial numerators a(c−b)/(c(c+1)), (b+1)(c+1−a)/((c+1)(c+2)), …, after the substitution b = γ−β (my identification). So K(α,β,γ) = F(α,γ−β+1;γ+1;x)/F(α,γ−β;γ;x). By Euler's transformation this equals F(γ+1−α,β;γ+1;x)/F(γ−α,β;γ;x).
The continued fraction on the right is the same form with α→γ−α and β→γ−β. Its partial numerators are (γ−α)(γ−β)/(γ(γ+1)), (α+1)(β+1)/((γ+1)(γ+2)), …
The claim is
K(α,β,γ) = γ(γ−α−β)/((γ−α)(γ−β)) + [αβ/((γ−α)(γ−β))]·K(γ−α,γ−β,γ).
I checked it by hand:
- Order x^0: (γ²−γα−γβ+αβ)/((γ−α)(γ−β)) = 1.
- Order x^1: both sides give αβ/(γ(γ+1)).
- Order x^2: the condition k1+k2 = k1'+k2' reduces to (α+β−γ)/(γ+1) + (γ−α−β)/(γ+1) = 0.
In hypergeometric form (a=γ−α, b=β, c=γ) the identity is the contiguous relation
a(c−b)F(a+1,b;c+1) = c(a−b)F(a,b;c) + b(c−a)F(a,b+1;c+1).
It therefore links two of Gauss's continued fractions with reflected parameters.

(2) 'Indirect solution of the first order' (regula falsi / secant).
Trial x=a gives X=A, and x=a' gives X=A'. Linear interpolation gives
x = (aA'−a'A)/(A'−A), at which X=0.

(3) 'Indirect solution of the second order': two unknowns x,y and two functions X,Y.
There are three trial points (a,b), (a',b'), (a'',b'') with values (A,B), (A',B'), (A'',B'').
X and Y are taken to be linear, i.e. the two planes through the three points are intersected. The root is the weighted mean x = Σλ_i a_i (and likewise y). The λ_i solve Σλ=1, ΣλA=0, ΣλB=0, so they are proportional to the cofactors:
x = [(A'B''−B'A'')a + (A''B−B''A)a' + (AB'−BA')a''] / [(A'B''−B'A'') + (A''B−B''A) + (AB'−BA')].

(4) Polar form of the residual vector: A = R cos S, B = R sin S, and so on.
Then A'B''−B'A'' = R'R'' sin(S''−S'). Dividing numerator and denominator by RR'R'' gives
x = Σ [sin(S''−S')/R]·a + … over Σ sin(S''−S')/R + … .

(5) 'Ein spec. Fall' (a special case): A = a−a', A' = a'−a'', A'' = a''−a''', and the same for B.
My interpretation: the trial points are successive iterates a→a'→a''→a''' of a two-dimensional fixed-point map. The residual is X = x − φ(x).
The denominator becomes
D = A(B'−B'') + A'(B''−B) + A''(B−B')
 = (a−a')(b'−2b''+b''') + (a'−a'')(−b+b'+b''−b''') + (a''−a''')(b−2b'+b'').
Gauss writes exactly these three products and then regroups by a, a', a'', a''':
- a(b'−2b''+b''')
- + a'(−b+3b''−2b''')
- + a''(…)
- + a'''(−b…), which is left unfinished.
With one variable this construction is Aitken's Δ² extrapolation. In two variables it is a vector (Henrici-type) extrapolation from n+2=4 iterates.
The line 'a(a'b''−b'a'') − a(a'b'''−b'a''') − …' is a tentative expansion of the same determinant by 2×2 minors. Its leading factors are unclear.

(6) Right margin: quartic Gauss sum for p=5.
The note '1+2i' refers to 5 = (1+2i)(1−2i), and 2 is a square root of −1 mod 5.
The general form is P = ρ + ηρ^i − ρ^{-1} − ηρ^{-i}, where ρ is a primitive 5th root of unity, i=2, and η = ±√−1 is the value of the quartic character at 2.
Gauss starts squaring it (ρ·P = ρ² + ηρ^{1+i} − 1 − ηρ^{1−i}, …). He then specialises to P = ρ + ηρ² − ρ⁴ − ηρ³ and Q = ρ − ρ² + ρ⁴ − ρ³, the quadratic Gauss sum, equal to √5.
The target is P² = (Gaussian integer of norm 5)·Q. The correct value is the Jacobi sum J(χ,χ) = −1−2η, so P² = −(1+2η)Q for either choice η=±i.

(7) Loose figures (43507, 11126?, 10.6…, 409): unrelated scrap arithmetic.
errors: In the regrouping of the special case, the coefficient of a'' should be 2b − 3b' + b''' (from −(−b+b'+b''−b''') + (b−2b'+b'')). The page appears to read +2b − b' − 3b'' + 2b''', which is wrong. The four coefficients must sum to zero, and Gauss's version does not.
The coefficient of a''' is left incomplete; it should be −(b − 2b' + b'') = −b + 2b' − b''.

The line 'a(a'b''−b'a'') − a(a'b'''−b'a''') − a(a''b'''−b''a''') + a(a''b'''−b''a''')' is internally inconsistent as transcribed: the last two terms cancel and all prefactors are 'a'. It is either a slip or abandoned scratch.

Margin: as transcribed, 'Q(1−η) = P²' cannot be right, since N(1−η)=2 but N(J)=5. The correct relation is P² = −(1+2η)Q. Gauss probably wrote a form involving 1±2η; the transcription is likely faulty here.
Minor: the indices on '1+' and '1−' at the end of the continued fractions are not legible; they are only continuation markers.

results.what: Transformation between Gauss's continued fraction K(α,β,γ) and K(γ−α,γ−β,γ): K(α,β,γ) = γ(γ−α−β)/((γ−α)(γ−β)) + αβ/((γ−α)(γ−β))·K(γ−α,γ−β,γ), equivalent to a contiguous relation of 2F1
results.modern_name: Gauss continued fraction for ratios of contiguous hypergeometric functions; contiguous relation c(a−b)F = a(c−b)F(a+1,b;c+1) − b(c−a)F(a,b+1;c+1)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones generales circa seriem infinitam, 1812/13); Euler's transformation (1778)

results.what: Two-variable 'indirect solution' with three trial points, using cofactor (determinant) weights, plus a polar-coordinate form of the weights
results.modern_name: multivariate secant method (linear interpolation through n+1 points)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Theoria motus (1809), art. ~120; modern revival by Wolfe and Bittner (1959)

results.what: Special case in which the trial points are successive iterates (residual = difference of iterates), giving extrapolation of a 2D fixed-point iteration from four iterates
results.modern_name: vector Aitken Δ² / Henrici's method (vector Steffensen-type extrapolation)
results.usually_credited_to: Aitken (1926) for the scalar case; Henrici (1964) and Brezinski for the vector case

results.what: Square of the quartic Gauss sum mod 5: P² = −(1+2η)·Q with Q = √5
results.modern_name: g(χ)² = J(χ,χ)·g(χ²) (Jacobi sum relation) for quartic characters
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (unpublished biquadratic work); Jacobi (1827/1837); Eisenstein; Cauchy

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is material firmly associated with Gauss: his hypergeometric continued fraction (seen here in 1805, before the 1812 publication), regula falsi, the multivariate secant method of Theoria motus, and quartic Gauss sums. The mildly notable item is the 'special case' that turns the two-variable secant into an extrapolation of a fixed-point iteration from four successive iterates. This is essentially a vector Aitken/Henrici process, usually credited to the 20th century. It is, however, a natural corollary of his secant scheme and is left unfinished, with an arithmetic slip.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,x=symbols('a b c x'); s=lambda p,q,r,n: sum(rf(p,k)*rf(q,k)/rf(r,k)/factorial(k)*x**k for k in range(n)); simplify(expand(a*(c-b)*s(a+1,b,c+1,6) - c*(a-b)*s(a,b,c,6) - b*(c-a)*s(a,b+1,c+1,6)).series(x,0,6).removeO())==0
checkable.asserts: Contiguous relation equivalent to the continued-fraction transformation, checked through x^5

checkable.sympy: al,be,ga,x=symbols('alpha beta gamma x'); K=lambda A,B,G: 1/(1-A*B/(G*(G+1))*x/(1-(G+1-A)*(G+1-B)/((G+1)*(G+2))*x/(1-(A+1)*(B+1)/((G+2)*(G+3))*x/(1-(G+2-A)*(G+2-B)/((G+3)*(G+4))*x)))); simplify(series(K(al,be,ga) - ga*(ga-al-be)/((ga-al)*(ga-be)) - al*be/((ga-al)*(ga-be))*K(ga-al,ga-be,ga),x,0,3).removeO())==0
checkable.asserts: The page's continued-fraction transformation, truncated, agrees through order x^2

checkable.sympy: a,a1,A,A1,p,q=symbols('a a1 A A1 p q'); simplify((p+q*(a*(p+q*a1)-a1*(p+q*a))/((p+q*a1)-(p+q*a))))==0
checkable.asserts: The regula falsi formula is exact for a linear function X = p + q x

checkable.sympy: x0,x1,x2,y0,y1,y2,p,q,r,s,t,u=symbols('x0 x1 x2 y0 y1 y2 p q r s t u'); X=lambda x,y:p+q*x+r*y; Y=lambda x,y:s+t*x+u*y; A=[X(x0,y0),X(x1,y1),X(x2,y2)]; B=[Y(x0,y0),Y(x1,y1),Y(x2,y2)]; w=[A[1]*B[2]-B[1]*A[2],A[2]*B[0]-B[2]*A[0],A[0]*B[1]-B[0]*A[1]]; xs=sum(w[i]*[x0,x1,x2][i] for i in range(3))/sum(w); ys=sum(w[i]*[y0,y1,y2][i] for i in range(3))/sum(w); simplify(X(xs,ys))==0 and simplify(Y(xs,ys))==0
checkable.asserts: The second-order indirect solution gives the exact root for linear X, Y
A'B''−B'A'' = R'R'' sin(S''−S') in polar form
Correct regrouping of the special-case denominator; the a'' coefficient is 2b−3b'+b''' (not Gauss's 2b−b'−3b''+2b''')
The one-dimensional analogue of the special case is Aitken's Δ² formula
The quartic Gauss sum P satisfies P² = −(1+2η)Q for η=±i (both values ≈ 0)
The quadratic Gauss sum Q mod 5 equals √5

transcription_corrections: The left continued fraction's third partial numerator is (α+1)(β+1)/((γ+2)(γ+3)), preceded by '1 −' (the '1+' / '1−' marks are continuation signs, not part of the formula).
The words after 'Verwandlung' are unclear; the bracketed 'Iteh.' guess is doubtful.
Third line of the special-case products: read '(a''−a''')(b−2b'+b'')'; the parentheses around a''−a''' were omitted in the transcription.
The a'' coefficient is read as '+2b − b' − 3b'' + 2b'''' (as written by Gauss, though mathematically wrong); this should be checked against the image, since the correct value is 2b − 3b' + b'''.
The final margin relation is probably '−Q(1+2η) = P²' or a similar 1±2η form, not 'Q(1−η)'. The heading '1+2i' supports a factor of norm 5.
In the margin's general formula, the exponent i is an integer index (i=2, a square root of −1 mod 5), not the imaginary unit; η denotes the quartic character value ±√−1.
